title: Projective-bundle morphisms are proper
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. If $f$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], meaning that $X$ is isomorphic over $S$ to a closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal E)$ for a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal E$, then $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Lemma 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper), together with Lemma 01WB (lemma-characterize-locally-projective) and Definition 01W8 (definition-projective).

proof.text: Unpack [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] to obtain a finite-type quasi-coherent module E, a closed immersion i into the canonical relative Proj of Sym(E), and the equality f = i ≫ relProjHom. Apply [lem-trf-canonical-relative-proj-proper] to the canonical projection.

The closed-immersion and composition clauses of [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] make i proper and then make i ≫ relProjHom proper. Transport along the factorization equality to obtain properness of f.

proof_origin.place: Tags 01WB and 01WC: split off properness of the canonical relative Proj, then compose with the closed immersion.
